body.statement: For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), the law \(p\) is Markov to \(D\). Hence the intersection of the represented DAG Markov models with the exact oracle model is exactly \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and no graph-local Markov generator strengthens \(J_{\mathcal I}\) on this domain.
body.justification: This reduction prevents the minimum-edge promise from being mistaken for extra observed-law equations.
body.gap: Raskutti and Uhler define sparsest I-maps, but do not isolate the common-law model needed for cross-graph effects.
body.consumer: The algebraic certificate generator can omit redundant graph-local minors and report a smaller verified ideal.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted input \(\mathfrak u\), a table \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and a represented DAG \(D\in\mathfrak D\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}sparsest\text{-}dag\text{-}family}\), \(D\) is an I-map of \(\mathcal I\), which means
\[
   \operatorname{CI}(D)\subseteq\{c:\mathcal I(c)=1\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), for every \(c\) in the set on the right all determinantal minors in the block encoding \(c\) vanish at \(p\).  In particular, every conditional independence in \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\) holds under \(p\).  This is precisely the global Markov property of \(p\) with respect to \(D\).  Since this conclusion holds for each \(D\in\mathfrak D\),
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}
 \subseteq \bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D),
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap
 \bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D)
 =\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ},
\]
where \(\mathcal M(D)\) denotes the set of laws globally Markov to \(D\).  Finally, a graph-local determinantal generator encodes a member of \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\), hence is already one of the bit-one oracle minors in \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\).  Adjoining all such graph-local generators therefore neither changes the zero set on the declared domain nor enlarges the ideal generated by the chosen literal oracle minors.  This proves all three assertions.
